MP2 Setup Exercise — Context-Threshold Warning Hook\\n\\n**Course:** IPHS 400 Frontiers of AI, Kenyon College, Fall 2026 (Jon Chun)\\n**Where this goes:** Student manual, Part 1 (setup), right after the template repo is cloned and `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` has run.\\n**Time:** 20–30 minutes. **Token cost:** under 3% of a 5-hour window (the scripts cost nothing at runtime; hooks run outside the model).\\n**Rubric link:** Factor B, item B6 \\\"session hygiene\\\" (3 pts). The judge checks that the hook works and reads `docs/process/compaction-log.md`.\\n**Verified against:** Claude Code hooks and status-line docs as of 2026-09-22. Record your own version with `claude --version` in `notes/setup_check.md`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Why you are building this\\n\\nPocock's loop runs one ticket per fresh context: `/clear`, then `/implement #N`. Most tickets finish well inside one window. A long ticket does not, and a model working in a very full context forgets the ticket's acceptance criteria and starts to drift from the spec. The course rule is:\\n\\n- **Short ticket:** `/clear` before it. Nothing else.\\n- **Long ticket:** once context passes **50–60%**, `/compact` at the next **green test** (the end of a `/tdd` red-green-refactor cycle), never in the middle of a failing test, and always with a focus note.\\n\\nYou cannot follow that rule if you cannot see the number. This exercise gives you a live meter and a warning that fires at the right moment.\\n\\n## How it works\\n\\n```mermaid\\nflowchart LR\\n    CC[\\\"Claude Code session\\\"] -- \\\"session JSON on stdin<br/>(every refresh)\\\" --> SL[\\\"ctx_statusline.py<br/>prints: [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\\\"]\\n    SL -- \\\"writes\\\" --> ST[\\\".claude/state/ctx_&lt;session&gt;.json<br/>{pct: 47.2}\\\"]\\n    CC -- \\\"Stop event<br/>(end of every Claude turn)\\\" --> G[\\\"ctx_guard.py\\\"]\\n    ST -- \\\"reads\\\" --> G\\n    G -- \\\"first time over 50 / 60 / 80%\\\" --> W[\\\"⚠ systemMessage shown to YOU\\\"]\\n    CC -- \\\"PreCompact event\\\" --> L[\\\"ctx_compact_log.py\\\"]\\n    L -- \\\"appends\\\" --> LOG[\\\"docs/process/compaction-log.md<br/>(grading evidence)\\\"]\\n```\\n\\nThree facts from the Claude Code docs make this design work:\\n\\n1. **The status line already receives the context percentage** as `context_window.used_percentage` on stdin. The status line is the customizable bar under your prompt.\\n2. **A `Stop` hook fires every time Claude finishes a turn.** The end of a turn is where a natural boundary (a green test) happens, so that is when the warning should appear.\\n3. **A hook's `systemMessage` is shown to the user, not to Claude.** The warning talks to you, and does not pollute Claude's context.\\n\\nA hook cannot type `/compact` for you. Slash commands are yours. The hook only warns; you decide.\\n\\nEach herdr pane or terminal tab running Claude has its own `session_id`, so parallel sessions keep separate meters and never trip each other's warnings.\\n\\n## The four files\\n\\n| File | Job | Runs when |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_statusline.py` | Shows the meter; records the percentage | Every status-line refresh |\\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_guard.py` | Warns at 50 / 60 / 80% | End of every Claude turn (`Stop`) |\\n| `.claude/hooks/ctx_compact_log.py` | Logs each compaction and its focus note | Before every compaction (`PreCompact`) |\\n| `tests/test_ctx_guard.py` | Proves the logic works | When `/tdd` or `/code-review` runs the suite |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step 1 — Check Python\\n\\nIn Ghostty (macOS) or Windows Terminal (WSL2), inside your `iphs400-mp2-cms` folder:\\n\\n```bash\\npython3 --version\\n```\\n\\n**Expected:** `Python 3.9` or newer (the `uv` setup from the setup manual gives you 3.12).\\n**If you see `command not found`:** macOS runs `xcode-select --install`; WSL2 runs `sudo apt install -y python3`. Then retry.\\n\\n## Step 2 — Open the hook files\\n\\nThe template already contains all four files. Open the folder in VS Code:\\n\\n```bash\\ncode .\\n```\\n\\nIn the Explorer panel, expand `.claude/hooks/`. You should see `ctx_statusline.py`, `ctx_guard.py`, and `ctx_compact_log.py`.\\n\\n**If `.claude` is not visible:** VS Code hides nothing by default, but macOS Finder hides dot-folders. Use VS Code, or run `ls -la .claude/hooks` in the terminal.\\n\\n## Step 3 — Read the status-line script\\n\\nThis file is complete. Read it so you know what it does; you will explain it in your report.\\n\\n```python\\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"Status line for IPHS 400 MP2.\\n\\nClaude Code runs this script on every status-line refresh and pipes session\\nJSON to stdin. The script does two things:\\n  1. prints one line under the prompt:  [Opus] ctx 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░\\n  2. records the context percentage in .claude/state/ctx_<session>.json so the\\n     Stop hook (ctx_guard.py) can read it at the end of each turn.\\nIt must never crash: a broken status line hides the meter, nothing else.\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nimport json\\nimport os\\nimport sys\\nimport time\\nfrom pathlib import Path\\n\\n\\ndef project_dir(data: dict) -> Path:\\n    ws = data.get(\\\"workspace\\\") or {}\\n    return Path(\\n        os.environ.get(\\\"CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\\\")\\n        or ws.get(\\\"project_dir\\\")\\n        or ws.get(\\\"current_dir\\\")\\n        or os.getcwd()\\n    )\\n\\n\\ndef bar(pct: float, width: int = 10) -> str:\\n    filled = max(0, min(width, round(pct / 100 * width)))\\n    return \\\"▓\\\" * filled + \\\"░\\\" * (width - filled)\\n\\n\\ndef main() -> None:\\n    try:\\n        data = json.load(sys.stdin)\\n    except Exception:\\n        print(\\\"ctx ?\\\")\\n        return\\n\\n    model = (data.get(\\\"model\\\") or {}).get(\\\"display_name\\\", \\\"Claude\\\")\\n    pct = (data.get(\\\"context_window\\\") or {}).get(\\\"used_percentage\\\")\\n    if pct is None:\\n        print(f\\\"[{model}] ctx --\\\")\\n        return\\n    pct = float(pct)\\n\\n    session = data.get(\\\"session_id\\\") or \\\"default\\\"\\n    state_dir = project_dir(data) / \\\".claude\\\" / \\\"state\\\"\\n    try:\\n        state_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\\n        tmp = state_dir / f\\\"ctx_{session}.json.tmp\\\"\\n        tmp.write_text(json.dumps({\\\"pct\\\": pct, \\\"ts\\\": time.time()}))\\n        tmp.replace(state_dir / f\\\"ctx_{session}.json\\\")  # atomic swap\\n    except OSError:\\n        pass  # meter still prints even if the disk write fails\\n\\n    flag = \\\"  ⚠ compact at next green test\\\" if pct >= 60 else \\\"\\\"\\n    print(f\\\"[{model}] ctx {pct:.0f}% {bar(pct)}{flag}\\\")\\n\\n\\nif __name__ == \\\"__main__\\\":\\n    main()\\n```\\n\\n## Step 4 — Write the Stop hook's logic (the exercise)\\n\\nThe template ships `ctx_guard.py` with everything written **except the body of `decide()`**, which raises `NotImplementedError`. Do not change the tests or any other function.\\n```\\n\\n`/tdd` runs the tests, watches them fail, writes the code, and runs them again until they pass. That\ncatches a link that is relative but wrong on a nested route\n(e.g. `pages` from `/admin/pages/home` would become `/admin/pages/pages`).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom urllib.parse import urljoin\n\nTEMPLATES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / \"templates\"\nHREF = re.compile(r'href=\"([^\"]+)\"')\n\n\ndef _local_hrefs(html: str) -> list[str]:\n    return [h for h in HREF.findall(html) if not h.startswith((\"http\", \"#\", \"mailto:\", \"tel:\"))]\n\n\ndef test_no_root_absolute_hrefs_in_any_template():\n    offenders = [\n        str(p.relative_to(TEMPLATES))\n        for p in TEMPLATES.rglob(\"*.html\")\n        if re.search(r'(href|src)=\"/', p.read_text())\n    ]\n    assert offenders == []\n\n\ndef test_dashboard_links_resolve(client_as):\n    manager = client_as(\"admin\")\n    url = \"/admin/dashboard\"\n    links = _local_hrefs(manager.get(url).text)\n    assert links, \"dashboard should link to the pages list for a Manager\"\n    for href in links:\n        assert manager.get(urljoin(url, href)).status_code == 200, href\n\n\ndef test_pages_list_links_resolve_including_nested_routes(client_as):\n    manager = client_as(\"admin\")\n    url = \"/admin/pages\"\n    links = _local_hrefs(manager.get(url).text)\n    resolved = {urljoin(url, h) for h in links}\n    assert \"/admin/pages/new\" in resolved\n    assert \"/admin/pages/home\" in resolved  # It runs a complete WordPress in your browser tab. Nothing installs; closing the tab wipes it. Break whatever you like.\n\nDo all six, in order:\n\n1. Write a **post**: title, a paragraph, **Save draft**. Visit the public site in another tab — it is not there.\n2. **Publish** it. Reload the public site — now it is.\n3. Write a **page** (\"About\"). Notice where pages show up that posts do not: the navigation menu.\n4. Open **Settings → Permalinks**. Look at how the URL is built from the title. That string is the *slug*.\n5. **Users → Add New**: create a user with the **Editor** role. Log out, log in as them. Try to reach **Users**. Write down exactly what happens.\n6. Find where **Posts → All Posts** lets you filter by status. That screen is the content list you will build.\n\n### 2.2 Write your field notes\n\nCreate `notes/cms-field-notes.md` with **at least five** observations *in your own words*. See `notes/client-brief.md`\nand `notes/restaurant-research.md` for the sourcing and reasoning behind each decision.\n\n| Term | Meaning in this project |\n|---|---|\n| **La Once Mil** | The site's display name — the restaurant's own verified branding. Supersedes the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used before this session, which was not an intentional name choice. |\n| **Flagship location** | The one restaurant location this project models: Monte Everest 780, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City — the Michelin-starred address. Roma Norte and Madrid locations are explicitly out of scope and must never appear on the site. |\n| **Demo Manager** | The seeded **admin** account for grading. Fictional — does not represent the real owner (César de la Parra) or any real staff. Can create/edit/delete Pages, manage users, and publish. |\n| **Demo Editor** | The seeded **editor** account for grading. Fictional. Can create and edit **News** drafts only — cannot publish, cannot reach Pages, cannot manage users. |\n| **Pages** | The site's \"Pages\" capability — same fields and admin-only create/read/update/delete operations as News/Posts (title, slug, Markdown body, status, author, timestamps), plus appearing in public navigation once published. Home, Menu, and Our Story are La Once Mil's seeded starting content (`scripts/seed_demo.py`), not a fixed limit — the Manager can add or remove Pages beyond them. Corrected 2026-09-29: an earlier decision called these \"fixed, not freely creatable,\" which conflicted with the MP2 rubric/manual's \"Pages: same operations as posts\" requirement (see spec #1). |\n| **News** | The site's \"Posts\" capability — draft/published announcements with title, slug, Markdown body, author, timestamps. Editor drafts; admin publishes. |\n| **Publish** | The admin-only action that marks a draft (News post or a permanent page edit) as published **in the local CMS**. The editor role cannot perform this action under any content type. Publishing is not the same as the public site updating — the GitHub Pages site only reflects the change after `cms publish` exports to `site/` and that export is deployed. |\n| **Navigation reachability** | Every published page, including Home, must be reachable by clicking through the public site's navigation — no published page is an orphan with no link pointing to it. |\n| **Visiting information** | Verified address, hours, a directions link, and a prominent Call button — lives entirely on Home. There is no separate Visit Us page. |\n| **Menu (page)** | One ordinary Markdown permanent page listing dish names and descriptions. No prices (no verified peso pricing exists) and no structured menu/pricing database — deliberately out of scope. |\n| **Placeholder image** | A clearly labeled stand-in image (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) used until a real, rights-cleared photo is supplied. Tracked in `notes/client-brief.md`'s image tracker. Never substituted with AI-generated or stock images. |\n| **Michelin item** | The one real, dated news item seed content may include — the Michelin star announcement — because the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the flagship (Lomas de Chapultepec) address specifically. Any other seeded News content is invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo. |\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":13,"oldLines":7,"newStart":13,"newLines":7,"lines":[" | **News** | The site's \"Posts\" capability — draft/published announcements with title, slug, Markdown body, author, timestamps. {"parentUuid":"0ce08365-f450-4dda-9d67-5b529e4f2458","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"92331d5e-7c1a-4d71-8037-d27ef11ad849","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016b831pY111SyAEVqdpE6Ma","type":"tool_result","content":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n----\n## Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\n`cms publish` exports only published content from the CMS to static `site/` HTML\nwith relative paths and working navigation, and `cms deploy` pushes it to\n`gh-pages`, giving a real Pages URL that serves the Home page.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] `uv run cms publish` writes `site/` with Home (and any other published\n      permanent pages) rendered from the database, replacing the current hard-coded\n      empty-items placeholder.\n- [ ] Every `href=`/`src=` in the exported HTML is relative; zero root-absolute\n      paths.\n- [ ] A page left in draft status is never written to `site/` — verified by\n      publishing with one page still in draft.\n- [ ] Every published page, including Home, is reachable by following links in the\n      exported HTML — no orphan pages.\n- [ ] `uv run cms deploy` pushes `site/` to the `gh-pages` branch; the Pages URL\n      serves the Home page over HTTPS.\n- [ ] `tests/test_publish.py` extends the existing T00 publish tests to cover\n      draft-excluded-from-export, relative-paths, and nav-reachability against real\n      Page content (not the placeholder).\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #3 (T02: Permanent pages) — needs real Page content and a status field to export\n  and to test draft-exclusion against.\n\n----\naccessibility bug documentation duplicate enhancement good first issue help wanted invalid question wontfix ready-for-agent spec ticket stretch \nusage: usage_report.py [-h] [--ledger LEDGER] [--remaining REMAINING]\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help            show this help message and exit\n  --ledger LEDGER\n  --remaining REMAINING\n                        tickets not yet built","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"86f32aa8-c139-4f07-b978-565cb944c953","timestamp":"2026-09-29T19:30:08.731Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. I read `git diff HEAD` and the four untracked files, and grepped `app/publish.py` and the routes for context.\n\n1. `templates/admin/pages_list.html:4` — Low. The links `pages/new` and `pages/{{ slug }}` only work when the list is served at exactly `/admin/pages`. Starlette's `redirect_slashes` only redirects `/admin/pages/` to `/admin/pages` if no route matches it first. If `/admin/pages/` is ever hit directly, the links resolve to `/admin/pages/pages/new` and 404. The same applies to `dashboard.html:6` if that page is ever served with a trailing slash. This is the cost of switching to relative links here. `rel('/admin/pages/new')` would avoid it.\n\n2. `templates/admin/dashboard.html:9`, `templates/admin/pages_list.html:8` — Low. The form actions (`/logout`, `/admin/pages/{{slug}}/delete`) are still root-absolute, while every href in the same files became relative. The checks only match `(href|src)=\"/`, so these pass. If the \"relative paths only\" constraint is meant to cover admin templates, these forms slip through. If it isn't, the mixed style is confusing.\n\n3. `app/urls.py:26` — Low. `_rel` reads `context[\"request\"]`, which raises `KeyError` if any admin template is rendered without a request in its context. The `TemplateResponse(request, ...)` form injects it, so today's callers are fine. A new caller that renders `base_admin.html` another way would get a 500 with a confusing message.\n\n4. `tests/test_admin_links.py:24` — Low. `_local_hrefs` deliberately skips the header links, so the header link on nested pages is never checked here. `test_admin_shell.py` covers that gap for four URLs, but not for `/login` or `/admin`.\n\n5. `app/main.py:31` — Info. `/admin/style.css` is served with no auth and no cache headers. It only exposes the public stylesheet, so this is harmless. Do not create it\nuntil every Stage 1 item below is complete and checked.**\n\n## Completed today\n\n- **First live deploy (closes T03's deferred criterion).** Seeded the empty Home,\n  Menu, Our Story pages (they were empty drafts in `cms.db`), ran `cms publish` and\n  `cms deploy`. Live and verified over HTTPS:\n  https://algoal0507-crypto.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ (index, menu, our-story,\n  style.css all 200).\n- **Site title** set to \"La Once Mil\" (`CMS_SITE_TITLE`, quoted in the untracked\n  `.env`; the malformed line is fixed). The app does not load `.env` itself: run the\n  CLI as `uv run --env-file .env cms publish` / `cms deploy`.\n- **Fake phone removed** (`tel:+00000000000` \"Call us\") from the seed and the DB row;\n  no verified number exists in the research sources. `CONTEXT.md` records the Call\n  button as pending. Photo placeholders were kept, as agreed.\n- **T08 / issue #9 (closed, commit `e41a99a`):** admin pages now load their\n  stylesheet and header link from any route depth (`app/urls.py`,\n  `templates/admin/base_admin.html`, `/admin/style.css`). Also made the admin `href`s\n  the checker flagged relative. Form `action=` attributes were deliberately left\n  alone. TDD, `/code-review` findings and resolutions posted on #9 and #4.\n  79 tests pass.\n- **Process evidence committed (`2df7145`):** transcripts 01–06 renamed from\n  `your-name` to `alejandro-gonzalez` (contents byte-identical), usage ledger,\n  `docs/process/compaction-log.md` (states from evidence that no compaction events\n  exist), `.gitignore` (`.gstack/`).\n- `CMS_STUDENT=Alejandro-Gonzalez` set in `.env`. Filenames are lowercase because the\n  checker's regexes require lowercase.\n- Secrets review: no real secrets in any committed file. `.env` is untracked and\n  still holds the template default values (`change-me-…`).\n\n## Stage 1 status\n\nChecker (`uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 1`): 11 of 12 pass; the\nonly failure is the missing tag, which is intentional. Passing the checker is **not**\nenough. Still incomplete against the rubric/manual:\n\n1. **S1.1 field notes — UNFINISHED (3 of 5 observations).** See below.\n2. **Token budget plan — UNFINISHED.** `notes/token-budget-plan.md` holds real ledger\n   data and is explicitly labelled as written on 2026-09-29, after T01–T03 (not\n   backdated). All model/effort/estimate cells and the three written answers are\n   marked UNFINISHED and need Alejandro's decisions.\n3. **S1.3 grill transcript — needs a decision.** Transcript 03 contains a\n   `mattpocock-skills:grilling` invocation plus `to-spec` and `to-tickets`. No saved\n   transcript contains the literal `/grill-with-docs` command, and none has a\n   `/research` session. Do not claim otherwise; consider telling the instructor.\n4. **Transcript 07 (this session)** is saved by the `SessionEnd` hook only when the\n   session actually ends, so it is **not yet in the repo**. After closing, run\n   `git status`; a new `..._07_alejandro-gonzalez_20260929.md` should appear\n   untracked. Check it for secrets, then commit it.\n5. Re-check S1.4–S1.7 once more just before tagging (spec issue #1, tickets #2–#8\n   plus #9, T01–T03 closed with review comments, Pages live with no absolute paths).\n6.
